[.claude/commands/pr-appr-resolve.md#scope]

## Scope

- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a PR number, use that
- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a repo (e.g., `bootstrap`), resolve comments on that repo's PR
- Otherwise, detect the current repo and find the open PR for the current branch
- **This Command is the single source of truth for the triage → present-plan → reply → resolve mechanics** — the Resolve Plan table format, reply templates, and thread-resolution GraphQL calls below. A `pr-manager` Agent, where one exists for the repo (`.github/agents/pr-manager.agent.md`), reads and applies steps 3-8 and 10 of this Workflow directly rather than duplicating them (skipping step 9 - commit and push remain /eap-git's and /eap-push's job, never the Agent's), the same way a Workflow references a Skill by canonical path (STD-TEC-AI-004 MR-7) or delegates to another Workflow as the single source of truth for shared logic (STD-TEC-AI-004 MR-9.5, Recommended Practice #1). This is not Agent-to-Agent subagent composition (STD-TEC-AI-002 MR-10) and not a Workflow invoking an Agent (no such mechanism exists) — it is simply an Agent reading a Workflow's documented procedure and executing it, identical in kind to how it would read a Skill. See the note after step 2 for how `pr-manager` feeds its taxonomy-classified findings into step 3 onward.

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-resolve.md#workflow]

## Workflow

1. **Pull latest** — run `git pull` to ensure you're working on the latest code before making any changes

2. **Identify the PR**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a PR number or repo name
   - If no PR specified, find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr list --head $(git branch --show-current) --json number --jq '.[0].number'`
   - If multiple repos specified (e.g., "both", "bootstrap and this"), process each

   > **Note for `pr-manager`:** When this Workflow is applied by `pr-manager`, the PR is already identified and its review threads already fetched (paginated) by that Agent's own steps — skip straight to step 3 using that data rather than re-fetching here.

3. **Fetch all review comments — paginated, never a single page**

   The REST comments endpoint defaults to 30 results per page and truncates silently past that with no error; a PR with more than 30 review comments will otherwise lose the remainder. Always use `--paginate`:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments --paginate \
     --jq '.[] | {id, path, line: (.line // .original_line), body}'
   ```

4. **Triage each comment** — decide whether to fix or not:

   | Decision | When | Action |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | **Fix in code** | Comment is valid and the fix improves the PR | Apply the fix, reply with what changed |
   | **Won't fix — intentional** | The code is correct by design (e.g., permissions policy, architecture choice) | Reply explaining the reasoning |
   | **Won't fix — already addressed** | The code already matches the suggestion, or the file was deleted/moved | Reply explaining what the diff shows |
   | **Won't fix — pre-existing** | Issue exists in code not changed by this PR | Reply noting it's pre-existing and out of scope |
   | **Won't fix — disagree** | The suggestion would make things worse or doesn't apply | Reply explaining why |

   **Every comment gets a reply. Every thread gets resolved — except a `pr-manager`-escalated finding the user explicitly chooses to leave open (see the note below).** Code changes are optional.

   Before deciding **Fix in code**, read `.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md` and apply its occurrence-inventory and cross-file-propagation methodology — a flagged line is a symptom of a concept, not the full extent of the fix. Before posting any replies or resolving any threads, run that Skill's Phase 4 checklist across the full PR diff — per that Skill's Phase 2 scope note, "changed files" means every file in the PR diff across all commits, not only the files this pass edits or the files with open comments.

   > **Note for `pr-manager`:** All of its findings arrive here **pre-decided** — the EA-artifact, AI-construct, and PR-metadata buckets as "Fix in code — done," with the fix already applied and a reply drafted from what the sub-agent (or `pr-manager` itself, for PR metadata) reported; its out-of-taxonomy bucket as either "Won't-fix" (trivial/cosmetic findings) or "Escalate — needs human review" (findings that appear to be genuine, potentially significant defects `pr-manager` cannot author a fix for). Do not re-triage any of them — carry them straight into step 5's plan. This step's own Fix/Won't-fix judgment applies only when a human invokes this Command directly, without `pr-manager`.

5. **Present the plan to the user for approval before posting**

   Display the triage locally as a table:

   ```text
   ## Resolve Plan — PR #{number}

   | # | File:Line | Decision | Reply |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 1 | src/auth.py:42 | Fix in code | Fixed — added input validation |
   | 2 | config.yml:8 | Won't fix — intentional | Intentional — matches team policy |
   | 3 | setup.sh:518 | Won't fix — pre-existing | Pre-existing, not changed in this PR |
   ```

   Then ask once:

   ```text
   Reply to {N} comments, fix {M} in code, and resolve all threads?
   ```

   - **User approves** — execute the plan (apply fixes, post replies, resolve threads — except a row marked "Escalate — needs human review" that the user chooses to leave open)
   - **User edits** — adjust per their feedback, then execute (no second approval round)

   **Do not post replies or resolve threads until the user confirms.**

6. **For comments you fix:**
   - Read the referenced file and line
   - Apply the fix using Edit tool
   - Reply to the comment thread:

     ```bash
     gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments \
       -f body="Fixed — <description of what changed>" \
       -F in_reply_to={comment_id}
     ```

7. **For comments you won't fix:**
   - Reply with a clear, specific reason (not just "won't fix")
   - Be professional — acknowledge valid points even when declining

8. **Resolve all threads via GraphQL — paginated, never a single page**

   The `reviewThreads` connection silently truncates at whatever `first:` page size you request, exactly like the REST comments endpoint in step 3 and the same connection `pr-manager.agent.md` step 2 paginates — a `first: 100` query on a PR with more than 100 threads returns exactly 100 with no error, and the remaining threads are never surfaced as unresolved. Always loop to `hasNextPage: false` before resolving. Exclude from the resolve list any thread the user explicitly chose to leave open under an "Escalate — needs human review" disposition (see step 4's note for `pr-manager`):

   ```bash
   # Page 1 — no cursor
   gh api graphql -f query='{
     repository(owner: "{owner}", name: "{repo}") {
       pullRequest(number: {number}) {
         reviewThreads(first: 100) {
           pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
           nodes {
             id
             isResolved
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }' --jq '{ids: [.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[] | select(.isResolved == false) | .id], hasNextPage: .data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage, endCursor: .data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.endCursor}'

   # Repeat with after: "{endCursor}" from the previous page, accumulating unresolved ids,
   # until hasNextPage is false:
   gh api graphql -f query='{
     repository(owner: "{owner}", name: "{repo}") {
       pullRequest(number: {number}) {
         reviewThreads(first: 100, after: "{endCursor}") {
           pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
           nodes {
             id
             isResolved
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }' --jq '{ids: [.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[] | select(.isResolved == false) | .id], hasNextPage: .data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage, endCursor: .data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.endCursor}'

   # Once every page has been fetched and all unresolved ids accumulated, resolve each:
   gh api graphql -f query='mutation {
     resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "{id}"}) {
       thread { isResolved }
     }
   }'
   ```

9. **Commit and push** if any code changes were made — `pr-manager` skips this step itself (it does not perform git operations, per its own Scope Boundaries) and instead reminds the user to run `/eap-git` and `/eap-push` separately.

10. **Report results:**

    - How many comments were reviewed
    - How many were fixed in code
    - How many were resolved as already-addressed or out-of-scope
    - Any that couldn't be resolved (explain why)

[.claude/commands/pr-appr-resolve.md#reply-templates]

## Reply Templates

**Fixed in code:**

```text
Fixed — <specific description of the change made>.
```

**Already addressed:**

```text
Already fixed in this PR — <explain what the diff shows>.
```

**Pre-existing, out of scope:**

```text
Pre-existing code, not changed in this PR. Noted for future work.
```

**Intentional design choice:**

```text
Intentional — <explain the reasoning>.
```
page_texts.5:
[.claude/commands/pr-appr-resolve.md#examples]

## Examples

```text
/pr-appr-resolve
```

Finds the PR for the current branch, reviews all comments, fixes what's actionable, replies, and resolves.

```text
/pr-appr-resolve 3
```

Reviews comments on PR #3 in the current repo.

```text
/pr-appr-resolve bootstrap
```

Reviews comments on the open PR in eap-bootstrap.

```text
/pr-appr-resolve both
```

Reviews comments on PRs in both the current repo and eap-bootstrap.

$ARGUMENTS
